topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

rows.title: Growth and yield of French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) under organic farming
rows.treatment_description: T1: 25% recommended dose of N through FYM (organic)
rows.control_description: T5: Conventional practice (Recommended FYM @25t/ha + Recommended NPK fertilizers)
rows.notes: Pooled data of 4 years, Year x Treatment interaction not significant. CD(P=0.05) = 0.76 t/ha applies across all treatments. Organic plots received FYM enriched with biofertilizers + rock phosphate + neem cake. T1 received 25% RDN through FYM plus base 25t/ha FYM.

rows.title: Growth and yield of French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) under organic farming
rows.treatment_description: T2: 50% recommended dose of N through FYM (organic)
rows.control_description: T5: Conventional practice (Recommended FYM @25t/ha + Recommended NPK fertilizers)
rows.notes: Pooled data of 4 years. CD(P=0.05) = 0.76 t/ha. T2 received 50% RDN through FYM plus base 25t/ha FYM.

rows.title: Growth and yield of French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) under organic farming
rows.treatment_description: T3: 75% recommended dose of N through FYM (organic)
rows.control_description: T5: Conventional practice (Recommended FYM @25t/ha + Recommended NPK fertilizers)
rows.notes: Pooled data of 4 years. CD(P=0.05) = 0.76 t/ha. T3 yield (17.45) exceeds T5 (15.93) by 1.52 t/ha, which exceeds CD (0.76), so significantly higher than conventional. Organic outperforms conventional here.

rows.title: Growth and yield of French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) under organic farming
rows.treatment_description: T4: 100% recommended dose of N through FYM (organic)
rows.control_description: T5: Conventional practice (Recommended FYM @25t/ha + Recommended NPK fertilizers)
rows.notes: Pooled data of 4 years. CD(P=0.05) = 0.76 t/ha. T4 yield (17.77) exceeds T5 (15.93) by 1.84 t/ha, significantly higher than conventional. Highest yielding treatment in entire trial.

rows.title: Growth and yield of French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) under organic farming

rows.notes: Pooled data of 4 years. CD(P=0.05) = 0.76 t/ha. T6 is chemical-only conventional (no FYM). Difference of 2.36 t/ha exceeds CD. All organic treatments outperformed T6.
